title: Natural rational representations and coordinate comodules
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $G$ an affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], and $A=k[G]=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ with its canonical coordinate Hopf structure [def-sfb-affine-coordinate-hopf-algebra]. Let $V$ be any $k$-vector space, with scalar extensions $V_R=R\otimes_k V$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. A natural rational representation on $V$ is a family of group homomorphisms $r_R:G(R)\to\operatorname{Aut}_R(V_R)$ for all commutative $k$-algebras $R$, such that $(\alpha\otimes1)r_R(x)=r_T(G(\alpha)(x))(\alpha\otimes1)$ for every $k$-algebra map $\alpha:R\to T$ and $x\in G(R)$. Here $G(R)$ is the group of scheme morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}R\to G$ over $k$, using [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A coordinate comodule on $V$ is a $k$-linear map $c:V\to V\otimes_k A$ satisfying $(c\otimes1)c=(1\otimes\Delta)c$ and $(1\otimes\epsilon)c=1_V$, with the tensor associativity and unit identifications of [def-sfb-hopf-action-module-data]. The generic point $a\in G(A)$ is the inverse of the canonical affine isomorphism $G\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$. For a $k$-algebra map $x:A\to R$, its coordinate point is $\operatorname{Spec}R\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}x}\operatorname{Spec}A\xrightarrow{a}G$. The generic coaction construction of a natural representation $r$ is the $k$-linear map sending $v$ to $r_A(a)(1\otimes v)$ followed by the symmetry $A\otimes_k V\simeq V\otimes_k A$. These are definitions; no correspondence theorem is asserted here. All individual spaces, schemes and test algebras lie in one common universe, and natural families may lie in a containing universe. No finite-dimensionality, nonzero-space or finite-type condition is imposed.
